units.text: INT. SUPERMAN - CONTINUOUS
Consider, Senora: was not this true even when you lived on earth? When you were 70, were you really older underneath your wrinkles and your grey hairs than when you were 30?
units.name: DON JUAN

units.text: No, younger: at 30 I was a fool. But of what use is it to feel younger and look older?
units.name: THE OLD WOMAN

units.text: You see, Senora, the look was only an illusion. Your wrinkles lied, just as the plump smooth skin of many a stupid girl of 17, with heavy spirits and decrepit ideas, lies about her age? Well, here we have no bodies: we see each other as bodies only because we learnt to think about one another under that aspect when we were alive; and we still think in that way, knowing no other. But we can appear to one another at what age we choose. You have but to will any of your old looks back, and back they will come.
units.name: DON JUAN

units.text: It cannot be true.
units.name: THE OLD WOMAN

units.text: Try.
units.name: DON JUAN

units.text: Seventeen!
units.name: THE OLD WOMAN

units.text: Stop. Before you decide, I had better tell you that these things are a matter of fashion. Occasionally we have a rage for 17; but it does not last long. Just at present the fashionable age is 40--or say 37; but there are signs of a change. If you were at all good-looking at 27, I should suggest your trying that, and setting a new fashion.
units.name: DON JUAN

units.text: I do not believe a word you are saying. However, 27 be it.
units.name: THE OLD WOMAN

units.text: Whisk! the old woman becomes a young one, and so handsome that in the radiance into which her dull yellow halo has suddenly lightened one might almost mistake her for Ann Whitefield.
Dona Ana de Ulloa!
units.name: DON JUAN

units.text: What? You know me!
units.name: ANA

units.text: And you forget me!
units.name: DON JUAN

units.text: I cannot see your face.
units.name: ANA

units.text: He raises his hat.
Don Juan Tenorio! Monster! You who slew my father! even here you pursue me.
units.name: ANA

units.text: I protest I do not pursue you. Allow me to withdraw
units.name: DON JUAN

units.text: going.
seizing his arm.
You shall not leave me alone in this dreadful place.
units.name: ANA

units.text: Provided my staying be not interpreted as pursuit.
units.name: DON JUAN

units.text: releasing him.
You may well wonder how I can endure your presence. My dear, dear father!
units.name: ANA

units.text: Would you like to see him?
units.name: DON JUAN

units.text: My father HERE!!!
units.name: ANA

units.text: No: he is in heaven.
units.name: DON JUAN

units.text: I knew it. My noble father! He is looking down on us now. What must he feel to see his daughter in this place, and in conversation with his murderer!
units.name: ANA

units.text: By the way, if we should meet him--
units.name: DON JUAN

units.text: How can we meet him? He is in heaven.
units.name: ANA

units.text: He condescends to look in upon us here from time to time. Heaven bores him. So let me warn you that if you meet him he will be mortally offended if you speak of me as his murderer! He maintains that he was a much better swordsman than I, and that if his foot had not slipped he would have killed me. No doubt he is right: I was not a good fencer. I never dispute the point; so we are excellent friends.
units.name: DON JUAN

units.text: It is no dishonor to a soldier to be proud of his skill in arms.
units.name: ANA

units.text: You would rather not meet him, probably.
units.name: DON JUAN

units.text: How dare you say that?
units.name: ANA

units.text: Oh, that is the usual feeling here. You may remember that on earth--though of course we never confessed it--the death of anyone we knew, even those we liked best, was always mingled with a certain satisfaction at being finally done with them.
units.name: DON JUAN

units.text: Monster! Never, never.
units.name: ANA

units.text: placidly.

I see you recognize the feeling. Yes: a funeral was always a festivity in black, especially the funeral of a relative. At all events, family ties are rarely kept up here. Your father is quite accustomed to this: he will not expect any devotion from you.
units.name: DON JUAN

units.text: Wretch: I wore mourning for him all my life.
units.name: ANA

units.text: Yes: it became you. But a life of mourning is one thing: an eternity of it quite another. Besides, here you are as dead as he. Can anything be more ridiculous than one dead person mourning for another? Do not look shocked, my dear Ana; and do not be alarmed: there is plenty of humbug in hell (indeed there is hardly anything else); but the humbug of death and age and change is dropped because here WE are all dead and all eternal. You will pick up our ways soon.
units.name: DON JUAN

units.text: And will all the men call me their dear Ana?
units.name: ANA

units.text: No. That was a slip of the tongue. I beg your pardon.
units.name: DON JUAN

units.text: almost tenderly.
Juan: did you really love me when you behaved so disgracefully to me?
units.name: ANA

units.text: impatiently.

Oh, I beg you not to begin talking about love. Here they talk of nothing else but love--its beauty, its holiness, its spirituality, its devil knows what!--excuse me; but it does so bore me. They don't know what they're talking about. I do. They think they have achieved the perfection of love because they have no bodies. Sheer imaginative debauchery! Faugh!
units.name: DON JUAN

units.text: Has even death failed to refine your soul, Juan? Has the terrible judgment of which my father's statue was the minister taught you no reverence?
units.name: ANA
